title: PostgreSQL VACUUM

options.t: Its MVCC keeps old row versions (dead tuples) after UPDATE/DELETE; VACUUM reclaims them and prevents transaction-ID wraparound

answer: MVCC leaves dead tuples that must be cleaned up.
explanation: Autovacuum normally handles this; long-running transactions prevent cleanup and cause bloat. VACUUM also updates the visibility map used by index-only scans.

title: InnoDB storage
body: How does MySQL's InnoDB engine physically organise table rows?

options.t: As a heap with no order
In a clustered index on the primary key; secondary indexes store the primary key value

explanation: Because secondary indexes reference the primary key, a wide primary key makes every secondary index larger. Random UUID primary keys cause page splits, like random GUIDs in SQL Server.

title: Limiting rows
body: Which clause limits the number of rows returned in PostgreSQL and MySQL?
explanation: The ANSI form `OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY` works in PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Large OFFSETs are slow; prefer keyset pagination (`WHERE id > @lastId ORDER BY id LIMIT 20`).

title: Indexing JSONB
body: Which index type is typically used to speed up containment queries (`@>`) on a PostgreSQL JSONB column?
explanation: Generalized Inverted Indexes index the keys/values inside JSONB documents (also used for arrays and full-text search). B-tree indexes on expressions such as `(data->>'email')` suit equality lookups on a single path.
